sections.heading: Relationships
sections.body: *la pareja* (partner / couple), *el novio / la novia* (boyfriend / girlfriend; also groom / bride), *el esposo / la esposa* (husband / wife — *el marido / la mujer* in Spain), *salir con alguien* (to go out with, date), *enamorarse de* (to fall in love with), *estar enamorado de* (to be in love with), *ponerse de novios* (to start dating seriously), *casarse con* (to marry), *comprometerse* (to get engaged), *separarse, divorciarse*, *pelearse* (to fight / argue), *reconciliarse* (to make up), *llevarse bien / mal con* (to get along well / badly with).

sections.heading: Ser or estar: meaning changes
sections.body: Some adjectives change meaning with *ser* and *estar*. You saw a few in A2; here are more:

vocab: to go out with / to date
examples: They've been a couple for ten years.
She fell in love with her neighbor.
Mis padres se divorciaron cuando yo era niño.
My parents divorced when I was a child.
Se pelean mucho, pero siempre se reconcilian.
They fight a lot, but they always make up.
Me llevo muy bien con mi suegra.
I get along really well with my mother-in-law.
La tienda está abierta hasta las nueve.
The store is open until nine.
Es muy interesado; solo piensa en el dinero.
He's very self-interested; he only thinks about money.
